title: 8x10 Antique View Camera (Wet-Plate Collodion on Glass)
purpose: Authentic 19th-century wet-plate collodion process with swirling Petzval perimeter bokeh, chemical edge pour marks, silver metallic luminance, and brooding Southern Gothic mood.

sensor_and_optics.camera_system: 8x10 Antique Wood Field View Camera (Wet-Plate Collodion)
sensor_and_optics.sensor_type: 8x10 inch silver iodide collodion emulsion poured on glass (ambrotype/tintype)
sensor_and_optics.full_frame_equivalent: ~45mm normal field of view with characteristic optical perimeter curvature
sensor_and_optics.iso_base: ISO 1 equivalent wet collodion chemical sensitivity
sensor_and_optics.dynamic_range: 10 stops high-contrast silver collodion response with orthochromatic blue sensitivity
sensor_and_optics.shutter: Lens cap manual exposure (2-4 seconds duration)

lighting_and_exposure.primary_lighting: Overcast natural outdoor daylight or high-intensity skylight, brooding atmospheric key
lighting_and_exposure.light_transport: Orthochromatic light response, dark brooding tones, metallic silver highlight reflectivity, heavy optical corner vignetting

surface_rendering: Physical chemical artifacts: visible collodion pour marks, drying streaks, and silver nitrate halos along plate margins
Piercing central sharpness resolving iris catchlights and skin pores amidst swirling perimeter defocus
Silver-toned monochrome with deep obsidian shadows and luminous metallic silver mid-tones
depth_and_optics: Signature Petzval swirling radial bokeh and rapid optical fall-off toward plate corners
Severe optical field curvature: tack-sharp central sweet spot falling off into soft dreamlike aberration
Uncoated glass flare and organic low-contrast perimeter glow

execution_directive: Enforce wet-plate collodion photograph on glass, antique uncoated lens with soft uneven focus and dark vignetting, silver-toned monochrome, chemical pour marks and streaks at the plate edges, brooding atmosphere, made with an antique 8x10 camera and wet-plate collodion. Zero photographer names.
